changes: Scribe reinterpreted: 'lekhakamahīpatiputrena(!)' most naturally reads lekhaka-Mahīpati-putreṇa, 'by the scribe, son of Mahīpati'. The cataloguer's (!) marks only the dental -n- (for putreṇa), not an intrusive word. So the scribe is an unnamed son (new p3: scribe, lekhaka, residence), and Mahīpati (p2) is changed to relative_only.
Relation added: p3 son_of p2. The under_reign_of relation now runs from the actual scribe (p3) to the king.
Date: ce_approx filled with Madanapāla's approximate reign (c. 1143–1161 CE). No date in an era survives (lacuna).
Notes: Pāla king of Bihar/Bengal; 'śau-' is possibly a misreading of 'gauḍa-'; the residence/place reading is partial.

notes: The copy was made during the 'increasing victorious reign' of the Pāla king Madanapāladeva of Bihar/Bengal (c. 1143–1161 CE). The passage after 'abhilikhya' is lacunose ('(patrāṅke vāsi)....bhū....tyā'). It may have contained a regnal year or other date, but none can be read. The scribe's compound reads 'śrīmanto..nagaravāstavyaśaulekhakamahīpati(putrena(!))'. Most likely this is '…-nagara-vāstavya-[gauḍa?/śau-]lekhaka-Mahīpati-putreṇa', 'by the son of the scribe Mahīpati, resident of Śrīmanto..nagara'. The son is not named. The other parse, with Mahīpati himself as scribe, is less likely. It is also unclear whether 'lekhaka' describes the father or the son. 'śau-' may be a misreading (perhaps 'gauḍa-' or 'kāyastha'-type designation). The town name (residence of the scribe) is only partly legible. It is not explicitly stated as the place of copying, and the catalogue gives the place as illegible. The catalogue's '12th century' fits Madanapāla's reign. The figure 129 after chapter 4 is a cataloguer's or scribe's count, not a date.
